label: input token is s
explanation: Pure token detector: fires on every step whose input token is the letter s, in both the original and copy phases, and on nothing else (dev P=R=1.0, corr 0.99). It never fires on the delimiter or on any other token. Magnitude is highest (~0.99 of max) when s is the first token of the sequence (t=0) or the input just before <DEL>. It is lower (~0.6-0.8) for s elsewhere in the original phase and lowest (~0.55-0.7) for s fed back during the copy phase. Position, L and neighbouring tokens do not affect whether it fires.

issues: The label and predicate hold up. On the test split, in_tok == tok('s') scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, mass recall 1.0 and correlation 0.987. Misses with --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives. On dev, the feature fires on 100% of s inputs and on 0% of every other token, including <DEL>.

One magnitude claim in the explanation is wrong: s as the input just before <DEL> does not peak near max. With t == L-1 as the predicate, mass_recall / recall = 0.0862 / 0.0845 = 1.02x the average magnitude. That is about 0.70 of max (mean 0.473 / max 0.685, times 1.02), the same as s in the middle of the original phase (1.01x). The claim rests on one top example ('o h k q a i x e [s:1.00] <DEL>'). Other examples contradict it, e.g. 'j 1 3 a [s:0.67] v w', where the s at t = L-3 is no weaker than typical.

The only real magnitude peak is s at t=0: mass/recall = 0.1195 / 0.0833 = 1.43x, about 0.99 of max, matching the [s:0.99] in the examples. s in the copy phase is the weakest at 0.91x, about 0.63 of max, which is consistent with the explanation.
No systematic gaps by position, L, phase, neighbouring token or in_first. The first_tok == s lift (5.9x) is only because s appears at t=0 in those sequences.
